mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the risk-free rate used in equity valuation models, leading to higher present values of future cash flows and thus positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.2 percentage points within a month indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically triggers a flight to safety and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 1 month, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer spending and economic expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through improved corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS rise by >0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, high industrial production (INDPRO > 105) signals potential overheating and imminent monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO > 105 during late-cycle expansions, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer confidence and economic activity, which consistently drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through improved corporate revenue outlooks.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST rises by >0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3 percentage points within a month signals rising inflation pressures, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3pp in 1 month, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in payrolls (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a robust labor market, which typically boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS rises > 50k and UNRATE falls > 0.1pp in 1 month, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During active monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 5 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is rising (by >0.1pp in 1 month) during a tightening cycle, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.
